correctness.rationale: With no singleton equivalence classes, the full class set F can be any subset of the active class set D: realize D minus F by proper nonempty class intersections. The upper output is the closed neighborhood of D. The empty neighborhood occurs only for empty D; the full neighborhood permits all F by taking D to be the entire quotient. Any nonempty proper upper neighborhood contains one entire side and a nonempty proper subset of the other, which is necessarily its unique D. These disjoint cases give all coefficients and the stated total. The lower marginal is monic of degree m+n; after removing the full-neighborhood contribution and the constant as specified in the theorem, the two difference polynomials have positive leading coefficients and the larger degree is max(m,n)-1, including m=n=1. The profile therefore identifies the unordered widths, not within-class sizes. Independently enumerating 16,384 element subsets for side block sizes (2,3) and (2,3,4) gave 55 distinct pairs and lower coefficients (10,16,13,10,5,1); the reduced polynomial was 10+11s+3s^2.
